The microstructures mainly consist of gray lamellar colony, with bright white B2 phase at the lamellar colony boundaries and small-sized white phase (the area marked by red dashed circle) inside the lamellar colony. As Er content is 0.04at.%, microcracks are observed near the B2 phase and Ti2AlC particles.
As the Er content increases from 0.04at.% to 0.08at.%, the lamellar colony is significantly refined [Fig. 1(c)], with their average size decreasing from 57.9 μm to 25.6 μm.
The long needle-like morphology and clustered distribution of Ti2AlC particles also contribute to stress concentration.
The morphology of the Ti2AlC particles gradually transitions from long needle-like to short rod-like, and their distribution changes from a clustered aggregation pattern to a more uniform dispersion.

evidence.quote: As Er content is 0.04at.%, microcracks are observed near the B2 phase and Ti2AlC particles. These microcracks are formed due to interfacial stress caused by the mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients among the B2 phase, Ti2AlC particles, and the TiAl matrix [Fig. 1(a)].

When microcracks form at the boundaries of the lamellar colonies, the large difference in deformability between the ErAl3 phase and the lamellar colony leads to rapid crack propagation along the ErAl3 phase boundaries, ultimately accelerating the fracture of the TiAl alloy.

evidence.section: 4.1 Effect of Er content on microstructures
evidence.quote: Subsequently, β grains nucleate from the liquid phase at the sites of nanoscale Er2O3 particles and refined Ti2AlC reinforcing phases. The nucleation rate of β grains significantly increases, and the size of the β grains is greatly refined.

The improvement in compressive properties are attributed to significant changes in microstructures, including the notable refinement of the lamellar colony, precipitation of Er2O3 particles, load transfer effect of the refined Ti2AlC reinforcing phase, and solid solution strengthening of Er solutes.
